items.body: C86 Holdings has acquired The Face from Wasted Talent Limited . In a joint statement released on 26 May , the Singapore and London-based announcement confirmed that the iconic culture publication will now enter a new chapter under C86 Holdings. First launched in 1980, The Face became a defining voice across music, fashion, style, and youth culture. The title ceased publication in 2004 before being relaunched by Wasted Talent in 2019 as a digital platform and quarterly print magazine. Wasted Talent is a global music and lifestyle media company whose portfolio includes Mixmag , Kerrang! , and The Face . The company describes Mixmag as “the global authority on dance music,” while The Face is billed as “the original home of style.” Kuok Meng Ru , Founder and Principal of C86 Holdings, said: “Some brands matter more than others, and The Face is undeniably one of them. I want to thank Ian and the Wasted Talent team for trusting me with the stewardship of this very special brand as it enters its next chapter. The work now is to carry its legacy forward with the care and ambition the brand deserves.” Kuok is also the Group CEO and Founder of Caldecott Music Group , whose portfolio spans BandLab Technologies , NME Networks , and Vista Musical Instruments . Ian Flooks , Chairman of Wasted Talent, added: “Meng is someone I've known and respected for many years. He has a rare combination of genuine passion for culture and a proven entrepreneurial track record of starting, relaunching and nurturing iconic brands, and evolving them for the future. I have every confidence that The Face is in the right hands.” For updates from The Face , visit theface.com .

items.body: STARGLOW debut the explosive and power-packed music video for their gritty and edgy single ' Good Boys Anthem '. The track sees them fully evolve into a more solidified and versatile musical direction as they infuse evocative lyrics with genre-blurring melodies to create interesting sonic textures. 'Good Boys Anthem' is built on a foundation of searing rock-inspired guitar chords with raw and abstract shoegaze melodies. The track depicts the fragmented emotions that bubble up within youths as they navigate the unpredictable path of life. Members TAIKI and GOICHI contributed to the writing process, offering an intimate and honest exploration of vulnerability, pride, and human connection. Directed by Hiroshi Shinagawa , the music video is set in an abandoned warehouse with a dark and almost dangerous buzz in the air. The visuals unfold like a gritty action film as STARGLOW take on a more cinematic style with this project. With fight scenes set in the rain, it tells the story of friendship, brotherhood, and loyalty between five friends who try to stick together despite the forces of adulthood and overwhelming responsibilities trying to pry them apart. The release of 'Good Boys Anthem' falls into place with 2026 being a particularly eventful year for the group. Their two MUSIC AWARDS JAPAN 2026 nominations under the categories Best New Artist and Radio Special Award: Radio Rising Artist of the Year, and the announcement of additional arena dates for their ongoing STARGLOW 1st Fan Meeting -STAR CRUISE- tour , including shows at Yokohama Arena and GLION ARENA KOBE , solidify their position as one of J-pop's rising stars to watch. With 'Good Boys Anthem', STARGLOW continue to push the boundaries of their artistry, embracing a darker and more emotionally charged sound that highlights both their musical versatility and storytelling ambition. As the group’s momentum continues to build through major award nominations, expanding arena shows, and increasingly cinematic releases, STARGLOW are proving themselves to be one of the most exciting rising forces in the J-pop scene today.

items.body: Wuss embark on a reflective new chapter with ' May? ', exploring the wistful and introspective journey of life. Life is hardly ever a smooth road. Being full of ups and downs, it's a completely unpredictable rollercoaster ride. While life can feel like a never-ending cycle of failure, rejection, heartbreak, and despair, 'May?' spreads warmth like the sun peeking out from behind the clouds to reassure listeners that, eventually, the darkness turns to light. Rather than fixating on the pain and uncertainty, the indie rock quartet frames the chaotic flurry of emotions as a rainbow at the end of the storm, when you finally get a big breath above the surface, stopping you from getting caught in the undertow. Written by Brilyan Prathama Putra and Sabiella Maris , with lyrics fully penned by Sabiella, the track is inspired by personal moments of vulnerability and internal turmoil. The track's title, 'May?', ties to the idea of asking permission to embrace self-love and move forward beyond the struggles, growing stronger. The track blooms into a quiet conversation, confronting your own emotions to instil a sense of quiet determination and reassurance within one's soul. 'May?' leans into warmth and subtlety rather than grandeur, making the song feel more like a quiet source of comfort amid uncertainty than a bold declaration. With 'May?', Wuss transform vulnerability into something deeply comforting, reminding listeners that even life’s darkest moments can eventually give way to hope and healing. Through its heartfelt lyricism and warm sonic textures, the track stands as a gentle reassurance to embrace growth, self-love, and the uncertainty that comes with moving forward.

items.body: South Korean indie favourites JANNABI are finally heading to Singapore for the very first time. Presented by FriedRice Entertainment , the duo’s JANNABI 1st Asia Tour : Sweat & Stardust in Singapore will take place on 13 August at Capitol Theatre , marking the Singapore stop of the band’s first-ever Asia tour. Comprised of Choi Jung-hoon and Kim Do-hyung , JANNABI have become one of Korea’s most beloved indie acts thanks to their nostalgic chamber pop sound and emotionally resonant songwriting. Since debuting in 2014, the band have steadily built a devoted following through releases that explore themes of youth, love, and growth. View this post on Instagram A post shared by FriedRice Entertainment (@friedrice.live) The band are perhaps best known for their breakout hit ‘for lovers who hesitate’, which took home Song of the Year at the 17th Korean Music Awards in 2020. Their live performances have also earned acclaim for their immersive storytelling and distinct concepts, with their futuristic concert All the Boys and Girls 2125 winning the Grand Prize for Best Concert at the 12th EDAILY Culture Awards. Fans attending the Singapore show can also look forward to exclusive fan benefits. VIP ticket holders will receive priority entry to the standing pen, priority merchandise access, a JANNABI guitar pick, and a chance to win a signed concert poster. All ticket holders will also receive a commemorative postcard. Tickets go on sale from 2 PM (SGT) on 3 June via Ticketmaster Singapore .

items.body: The glitz and glamour of red carpet season rages on as the 52nd American Music Awards (AMAs) carpet receives some of the industry's rising stars and iconic legends for a night of recognition and celebration. This year's instalment of the awards spotlights more Asian artists, with several K-pop artists being nominated across categories outside of the usual Favourite K-pop Artist category . This year's awards feature two K-pop-specific categories, including Best Male K-Pop Artist and Best Female K-Pop Artist . The former category sees K-pop royalty such as ATEEZ , BTS , ENHYPEN , Stray Kids , and TOMORROW X TOGETHER nominated, with the latter category presenting an electrifying ensemble of the most fiery female groups, including aespa , BLACKPINK , ILLIT , LE SSERAFIM , and TWICE . Winners BTS However, Asian artists are not just confined to these two categories this year. This year marks a monumental moment with Asian artists winning among international nominees as well. Beginning with one of the biggest wins in a major category, BTS dazzles the crowd as their lead single ' SWIM ' from their comeback album ARIRANG won the Song of the Summer category. During their speech, RM shared, “Thank you so much for giving so much love to ‘SWIM’. When we made this album, we felt a lot of pressure and tried to figure out what kind of music felt the most like us right now. But the one thing we believed in was that we have to keep challenging ourselves and keep moving forward.” V then added, “To everyone out there who keeps swimming, we send you our love and support.” BTS accepts the award for Song of the Summer for "SWIM" at the #AMAs pic.twitter.com/UjTe8Lor11 — Variety (@Variety) May 26, 2026 Nominated against some of this year's most viral hits, like the shimmering allure of Harry Styles ' ' American Girls ', the sassy energy of PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson 's ' Stateside ', and even the haunting rhythm of Tame Impala and JENNIE 's ' Dracula '. That was certainly not the only time BTS would be on stage to accept an award, as they had a clean sweep, winning all the categories they were nominated for. They claimed their throne as the kings of K-pop as they won the award for Best Male K-Pop Artist. Rounding off their series of wins for the evening, they prove that they are not just a force to be reckoned with within the K-pop scene, but in the global music scene as well, claiming the coveted Artist of the Year award, marking a pivotal moment that reinforces their influence even after their temporary hiatus. RM thanked ARMYs once again for their support as he says, "...Our biggest thanks and gratitude always goes to ARMYs all over the world." Because of the fans, @bts_bighit is taking home the biggest award of the night! Congratulations on Artist of the Year at the #AMAs ! 🎉 pic.twitter.com/P9GJaZBpHV — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 HUNTR/X (EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami) Soaring through more extremely deserving wins, the air went still as the nominees were listed for the prestigious Song of the Year category. While everyone eagerly awaited to know which song soundtracked 2025 and 2026, the crowd erupted into cheers as the empowering anthem ' Golden ' from Netflix 's KPop Demon Hunters emerged victorious. The Singing Voices of HUNTR/X: EJAE, Audrey Nuna, Rei Ami are your Song of the Year winners for "Golden" 🎶 #AMAs pic.twitter.com/6P1R5VnwFq — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 ' Golden ' also triumphed in the beloved Best Pop Song category against an all-star lineup of nominees that included Olivia Dean , Sabrina Carpenter , and Taylor Swift . The bold voices of EJAE , Audrey Nuna , and Rei Ami also had their moment to shine as they took home the award for Best Vocal Performance . With 'Golden' having sparked a viral TikTok trend centred around attempting its legendary high note, their win in the category felt especially well deserved. Last but not least, after winning every category they were nominated in at the AMAs, the official KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack secured the Best Soundtrack award . Not only did the win highlight the film’s expansive global reach, but it also symbolised the continued growth of K-pop culture beyond borders as audiences around the world embrace its appeal. KATSEYE In the name of spotlighting global groups, KATSEYE stepped up onto the stage to accept their award for the New Artist of the Year category. During KATSEYE ’s acceptance speech, Sophia gave a heartfelt shoutout to BTS , thanking the group for inspiring them to represent their culture on a global scale. KATSEYE shouts out BTS for "inspiring us to represent our culture on a global scale" after winning Best New Artist at the #AMAs . (via CBS) pic.twitter.com/cDltrqc971 — Variety (@Variety) May 26, 2026 Known for their extremely vibrant and over-the-top visuals, KATSEYE also took home the amazing Best Music Video award for ' Gnarly '. "You could describe everything with one single word," and it would be awesome, as KATSEYE also had a clean sweep receiving the award for Breakthrough Pop Artist . Their wins are a testament to their rapid rise from their debut to dominating festival stages, and now winning awards with their explosive sonic style and undeniable ability to deliver hit after hit. TWICE One of the most monumental wins of the evening went to TWICE , who emerged victorious in the Best Female K-Pop Artist category. With their warm, lovable charm and confident flair, it comes as no surprise that the musical powerhouses clinched the award as they continue to carve out their own path and expand their artistry with each new release. Fans online rejoiced over the group’s win, flooding social media with congratulatory messages and celebrating the landmark moment. Iconic performances & moments The AMAs would not be complete without the reverberating beats of amazing performances. Select nominees staged amazing shows that got the crowd on their feet as they jammed out to some of the greatest hits on the charts right now. Needless to say, BTS delivered a powerful performance that served as a bold statement declaring, “We’re back, and we’re here to stay.” Still riding the high of their comeback era, they channel the passionate fire of ARIRANG , infusing their inner edge and rebellion as they opened the AMAs with ' Hooligan '. The striking track was the perfect way to kick-start the awards ceremony as its carefree nature was bound to spark excitement within the nominees and audiences. 📢 WATCH THIS WATCH THIS 📢 @bts_bighit goin' hooligan at the #AMAs Tune in NOW on @cbs and @paramountplus ! pic.twitter.com/l17LithXLp — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 BTS also took the stage later to present SZA with her AMA for the Best Female R&B Artist. During her speech, she expressed that it was nice to officially meet the powerhouse group formally in person, sharing, "It's crazy that this is the moment, so I had to take this moment to just let this be the moment." SZA fangirls meeting BTS at #AMAs pic.twitter.com/m9ydMYVSxJ — Deadline (@DEADLINE) May 26, 2026 Later on during the ceremony, the crowd got their ' PINKY UP ' as KATSEYE strutted onto the stage, performing their latest hit single with its booming techno rhythm that created an exhilarating sonic atmosphere within the arena. The quintet blew audiences away with their energetic choreography, making their performance one of the most memorable moments of the awards. KATSEYE performed “Pinky Up” at the AMAs tonight and completely owned the stage. KATSEYE GOES WILD AT AMAs #KATSEYE_AMAs pic.twitter.com/wiMvNw0DZ8 — KATSEYE B✶SE (@KATSEYEBASE) May 26, 2026 These victories mark a huge shift in the industry as Asian artists are increasingly being recognised on global stages, proving that their music, artistry, and cultural impact continue to resonate far beyond borders. From electrifying performances to landmark wins, this year’s American Music Awards reflected a growing era of inclusivity and international representation within mainstream entertainment.

items.body: BABYMONSTER are officially bringing their second world tour to Singapore this November, and ticketing details are finally here. The K-pop girl group will perform at the Singapore Indoor Stadium on 28 November as part of the 2026–27 BABYMONSTER WORLD TOUR ‘춤 (CHOOM)’ . The upcoming show follows the success of the septet’s sold-out Singapore concert in 2025 during their debut HELLO MONSTERS world tour. Organised by Live Nation Singapore , the concert marks one of the group’s Asia stops for the ongoing world tour, which will also see the act perform across cities including Bangkok, Jakarta, Kuala Lumpur, Taipei, Hong Kong, Sydney, and Melbourne. BABYMONSTER are currently promoting their third mini album, 춤 (CHOOM) , which was released on 4 May. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Live Nation SG (@livenationsg) Ticket prices for the Singapore concert are priced at S$358, S$348, S$308, S$298, S$258, S$228, S$188, and S$168, excluding booking fees. VIP ticket holders will receive: Priority entry for standing or seated sections Access to the pre-show soundcheck party A commemorative VIP laminate and lanyard Limited-edition VIP gift Exclusive photocard set MONSTIEZ MEMBERSHIP holders can register for the Weverse presale from 26 May, 12 PM to 29 May, 11:59 PM . The Weverse presale will then take place on 8 June , from 10 AM to 11:59 PM . Mastercard and Trip.com presales will run on 9 June , from 10 AM to 11:59 PM , while the Live Nation presale is set for 10 June , from 12 PM to 11:59 PM . General ticket sales begin on 11 June at 12 PM via Ticketmaster Singapore .

items.body: The Click Five are heading back to Singapore for another night of pop-rock nostalgia. Following two sold-out shows at Capitol Theatre in 2025, the American band are set to return with the 29 August stop of their For Lovers Tour at Arena @ EXPO . Known for defining the soundtrack of the early 2000s with irresistible hooks and singalong-ready choruses, the band’s upcoming Singapore show is expected to be their biggest one in the country yet. Fans can look forward to live performances of hits including 'Jenny', 'Just the Girl', and 'Catch Your Wave', alongside other fan favourites from across their catalogue. The Boston-formed outfit first built a massive fanbase across Asia during their original run, becoming one of Myspace’s most-viewed bands at the height of their popularity. Their 2025 Southeast Asia comeback tour reignited that connection with longtime fans, with tickets for their Singapore dates reportedly selling out within hours. As part of the For Lovers Tour , the band will also be offering VIP packages and experiences for concertgoers. items.body: Hans Zimmer is set to return to Singapore with his brand-new live production, Hans Zimmer Live – The Next Level World Tour 2026 , happening on 7 October at the Singapore Indoor Stadium . Presented by AEG Presents Asia , Semmel Concerts , and RCI Global , the upcoming show marks the legendary composer’s first performance in Singapore since 2019. Known for transforming film scores into immersive live spectacles, Zimmer’s latest production promises an even more ambitious cinematic experience, featuring electronic sound design, large-scale orchestration, spectacular lighting, and a brand-new stage concept. View this post on Instagram A post shared by AEG Presents Asia (@aegpresentsasia) Speaking about the tour, Zimmer shared: “I want fans to feel like they’re at a rave party or riding a roller coaster. For me, every show is a new voyage of discovery.” Fans can expect fresh arrangements from some of Zimmer’s most iconic film scores, including music from Pirates of the Caribbean , The Lion King , The Dark Knight , Interstellar , and Dune . The setlist will also feature selections from Dune: Part Two and F1®: The Movie . View this post on Instagram A post shared by AEG Presents Asia (@aegpresentsasia) The Singapore stop is part of Zimmer’s wider Asia run, which will also see the composer perform in cities such as Yokohama, Kaohsiung, Taipei, Beijing, Hangzhou, Chengdu, and Guangzhou. Tickets will go on sale via SISTIC on 2 June from 10 AM onwards.

items.body: Looking back on a glorious 11-year journey, the sun isn't setting anytime soon on SEVENTEEN as they celebrate their anniversary, sharing warm and heartfelt messages with CARATs on Weverse . Earlier this year, S.Coups , Jeonghan , Joshua , Jun , Hoshi , Wonwoo , Woozi , DK , Mingyu , The8 , Seungkwan , Vernon , and Dino all renewed their contracts with PLEDIS Entertainment , strengthening their bond with fans as they make a pledge to be their favourite idols for as long as they can. With many more milestone anniversaries on the horizon, CARATs celebrate this landmark moment by sharing clips of old performances and iconic moments that stay etched in their minds. As fans reminisce about the journey of the group so far, the members took to Weverse to share their messages of appreciation, joining in on the nostalgic reflection of the paths they've forged. Although he is currently serving his national service, Hoshi expresses his excitement to complete his duties and reunite with the band to continue performing and creating new bangers for fans to rock out to. The8 echoes a similar sentiment as he expresses his love by saying, "It’s been 11 years. Thank you for always being by our side, thank you to all the members for getting this far, it hasn’t been easy. Because of the time we’ve spent together, we've long become a part of each other’s lives. We hope to continue creating many more memories together in the future. Thank you for your unwavering love." As each member expresses their gratitude for the support from CARATs for the past 11 years, they look forward to an even more eventful future as SEVENTEEN. The group anticipates more new hits, even bigger performances, and new endeavours as they continue to preserve the original energy and passion that they have served up since their debut.

items.body: Lola Amour celebrated a decade of music with a sold-out two-night anniversary event at 123 Block in Mandaluyong on 22 and 23 May , drawing over 2,500 fans across the weekend for a heartfelt full-circle celebration of the band’s journey. Originally planned as a one-night show on 23 May, overwhelming demand prompted the addition of a “Pre-Game” night on 22 May — with both dates eventually selling out. Across the two evenings, fans were treated to performances from Any Name’s Okay , Jan Roberts , Shirebound , and The Ridleys , alongside a career-spanning set from Lola Amour themselves. Beyond the live performances, attendees also explored the Lola Amour Museum , an exhibit showcasing memorabilia from the band’s 10-year history. Among the featured pieces were the band’s 2017 Wanderband Champions trophy, their Japan Ruby Award from the 2025 Music Awards Japan, and the iconic “Shiela” costume from the ‘Raining in Manila’ music video. The anniversary weekend was packed with memorable moments that highlighted the band’s close relationship with its fans and collaborators. One standout performance saw Sof of Any Name’s Okay join the band for ‘Clarity’, while a chaotic and crowd-pleasing cover of ‘Mr. Brightside’ brought together Jan Roberts, Renzo of Any Name’s Okay, Ivo Impreso of PLAYERTWO , and former road manager Peter onstage. During the set, bassist Manu crowd-surfed through the audience, earning one of the loudest cheers of the weekend. Fans also witnessed a playful moment during ‘Lambing’, where frontman Pio transformed into a human disco ball with a mirrored helmet during the song’s instrumental break. The emotional high point of the celebration came during a reunion of the bands that would eventually form Lola Amour. Former members Raymond King and Martin Kim returned to perform as Decaf , while current trumpeter Angelo Mesina briefly returned to his original role as drummer. Joxx Perez and Renzo Santos also made surprise appearances as Sinigang Na Baboy. To close the weekend, all former members joined Lola Amour onstage for the final chorus of ‘Raining in Manila’, creating a powerful moment that encapsulated the band’s decade-long journey from playing small venues to becoming one of the Philippines’ biggest acts. Part concert, part reunion, and part tribute to the community that has supported them since the beginning, Lola Amour’s anniversary weekend felt less like a retrospective and more like a celebration of everything still ahead for the band.
